newsitem.title: UK: Dollar regains poise in Europe after tumble vs mark.
newsitem.headline: Dollar regains poise in Europe after tumble vs mark.

text.p: The dollar edged lower against the mark in late Europe after comments from Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer that the dollar's correction higher against the mark would end soon.

A spooked market sent the U.S. currency tumbling more than two pfennigs, compounded by profit-taking and stop-loss orders, dealers said. A surprising negative December U.S. durable goods orders figure put further downward pressure on the dollar before it regained nearly a pfennig against the mark.
"The market has calmed down after Tietmeyer's comments," said Peter Wood, dealer at Bank of Boston in London.
"I don't think it changes the underlying fundamentals for the dollar, which are pretty good for the moment."
The dollar sank to 1.6343 marks before rebounding nearly three-quarters of a pfennig to trade at 1650 GMT at 1.6425/35 marks, below its 1.6464/69 level in late Europe on Tuesday.
Some analysts said Tietmeyer's comments seemed to indicate a turnaround in the Bundesbank's policy.

"Everyone thought they were comfortable with these levels," said Lee Ferridge, currency strategist at Commerzbank in London. "The levels aren't really the problem, it's the speed of the move he's worried about."
Tietmeyer made the comments earlier today on the fringes of an official gathering in Bonn.
After soaring towards 123 yen, the dollar also retreated against the Japanese currency. It traded at 121.90/00, above its Tuesday 121.10/20 level in late Europe.
Japan's Minister of Finance Hiroshi Mitsuzuka released a series of comments on the yen's level, saying that Japan was watching movements in the currency markets closely.
He also said Japan would take appropriate measures towards any excessive moves, but added that recent moves resulted from the dollar's strength rather than the yen's weakness.
The dollar sunk to 1.6343 marks before rebounding nearly three-quaters of a pfennig to trade at 1650 GMT at 1.6425/35 marks, below its 1.6464/69 level in late Europe on Tuesday.
"They don't have as much influence in the market right now as the Bundesbank," said Ferridge.
Investors will be skittish ahead of next week's meeting of Group of Seven finance ministers in Berlin, dealers said.
"The mark and yen will be under the spotlight," Ferridge said, adding that the mark would be particularly watched after the Bundesbank's decision to express concern about its levels.
The dollar was also underpinned against the Swiss franc by comments by Swiss National Bank Chairman Hans Meyer that a weaker franc had helped growth, but the country's economy remained fragile.
The dollar traded at 1.4252/62 Swiss francs at 1710 GMT, nearly level with its European close at 1.4257/67.
U.S. December durable goods orders (excluding defence) fell 1.7 percent compared with a consensus estimate of plus 1.2 percent.
U.S. data due tomorrow include weekly jobless claims and money supply.
--Scott McCormack, London Newsroom +44 171 542 6762
